items.question: What is Sapiom?
items.answer: Sapiom is a San Francisco-based AI infrastructure startup that helps companies deploy and scale AI agents in production. Its platform dynamically routes each agent request to the most cost-effective model and compute path, enforces spending budgets before actions execute, and provides reliability through automatic failover. It offers three products: Sapiom Router (model routing), Sapiom Agent Studio (build and test environment), and Sapiom Runtime (managed production infrastructure).

items.question: How is Sapiom different from OpenRouter?
items.answer: Unlike OpenRouter, which acts as a middleman between developers and AI providers, Sapiom runs open-weight models on its own GPU racks in a San Jose data center. This lets it serve those models at direct compute cost rather than passing a provider markup through. For proprietary models like GPT-5.6 and Claude, Sapiom still routes through the originating provider, but substitutes a hosted open-weight model when quality thresholds allow.

items.question: What is the AI agent production gap?
items.answer: The agent production gap is the distance between a working AI agent demo and a reliable, cost-controlled production deployment. Building a demo with a frontier model API is straightforward. Keeping it running reliably at scale, without runaway inference costs, unpredictable latency, or provider outages, requires infrastructure most teams currently build from scratch. Sapiom targets that gap.
